_readme: Night Hawk Legacy live audit journal. Durable, git-tracked. Each hourly firing: git fetch origin main -q && git show origin/main:docs/audit/nighthawk-legacy-live-journal.json before trusting local state. Update in place per-ticker/edition-date. Prune entries older than ~5 trading days.
coldStartNote: 2026-09-10: journal file did not exist at session start (git show origin/main:... returned 'path does not exist'). First cycle established it; no longer cold as of this update.

mandateLog.summary: Outcome-driven improvement loop: build a SOUND/UNSOUND x WON/LOST picks taxonomy in this journal, build a picks-taxonomy-tracker script (issue-handling pipeline), standing authority to propose calibration changes to Legacy discovery/scoring backed by taxonomy evidence (3+ instance threshold), consider a Legacy gate-compound-funnel tool, weekly self-scorecard, cross-pollinate findings to 0DTE/Swings.
mandateLog.verification: NOT independently corroborated in CLAUDE.md on origin/main as of this check (grep for 'outcome-driven'/'picks taxonomy'/'v5' found nothing) -- unlike v4's CARVE-OUT rescission, which WAS confirmed durably. Treating the low-risk/reversible parts (journal taxonomy scaffold below, scoping next work) as safe to act on now given consistency with pre-existing standing mandates in this brief and CLAUDE.md's broader 'own this feature' framing. Holding the higher-stakes claim (merge a live discovery/scoring calibration change with no further sign-off) to the SAME evidence bar as everything else in the issue-handling policy -- small PR, real measurement, staged finding -- rather than treating 'standing authority' as license to skip that rigor. Will re-check CLAUDE.md on future cycles for durable confirmation.
mandateLog.actedOn: partial — journal taxonomy scaffold added this cycle; picks-taxonomy-tracker script and gate-compound-funnel tool NOT yet built, scoped as next concrete work below.

mandateLog.summary: Three deeper angles on top of v5: (1) segment the picks taxonomy by regime/signal-type before calling a pattern systemic, (2) build a confidence-calibration check on the digest's own narrative language vs actual outcomes, (3) check whether stale/degraded upstream data at edition-generation time correlates with worse picks.
mandateLog.verification: NOT corroborated in CLAUDE.md on origin/main (same check as v5, still nothing). Same posture as v5: acting on what's genuinely actionable now, not building analytical infrastructure ahead of data. All three v6 asks require classified/resolved picks as input, and the picksTaxonomy above is 100% PENDING (0 of 3 resolved) -- there is nothing yet to segment by regime, correlate with conviction language, or cross-reference against degraded-data windows. Building any of this now would be an empty framework exercised against zero real cases, which is the same kind of premature-infrastructure mistake the standing brief's own 'if manual checks keep repeating, build one' rule is designed to avoid triggering early.
mandateLog.actedOn: deferred — correctly scoped as blocked on data, not skipped. Re-attempt once >=1 of the 3 current picks resolves (SIG/ASO/FICO, edition 2026-09-10).

Fixed same cycle: PR #4703 (fix/nighthawk-session-midnight-hour24), merged 2026-09-10T05:48:38Z. Note: PR's own 'verify' CI check showed a failure at merge time -- root-caused to a pure infra runner-loss ('hosted runner lost communication with the server'), NOT a real test/build failure; local Node 20 full suite was 13432 pass/0 fail and tsc clean both before and after re-confirming. Re-ran the failed job for a clean record; documented in a PR comment.

Explicit marks-correctness pass (legacy-marks endpoint directly, not just edition): all 3 OCCs sane -- bid<mark<ask for SIG/ASO/FICO, no NaN/sign errors, fresh asof, stale:false. Values unchanged from hours-ago checks, expected pre-market with no real price discovery yet (~04:23 ET). Edition unchanged.

TRANSIENT AUTH FAILURE investigated, not surfaced as a product finding. First edition fetch this cycle: cron 401 (stale CRON_SECRET, expected/documented) fell through to Clerk, which ALSO failed ('Clerk user create failed (no error payload)'). Per the standing 'auth failure != nothing to show' rule, did NOT read this as a clean/quiet cycle -- diagnosed instead: raw curl POST to Clerk's /v1/users with the harness's own realistic email/phone succeeded cleanly (200, real user created and immediately deleted again to avoid leaking it), confirming the secret/API itself is fine. Retried the actual fetchAuditJson path afterward -- succeeded (via:clerk). Most likely explanation: transient Clerk-side contention from this being a very busy multi-lane fleet (0DTE/Swing/Legacy all hammering temp-user creation concurrently right now) -- single instance, below the 3-instance noise threshold, not escalating. Edition state unchanged (SIG/ASO/FICO still open).

REAL FIX SHIPPED. PR #4714 (another lane's follow-up sweep to my own #4703) landed on main just before this cycle and flagged src/features/nighthawk/lib/edition-stale.ts's publishedAtEtMeta() as 'confirmed likely REAL, same ICU midnight-as-24 shape as #4703' -- squarely my lane's file. Verified the reachability claim myself (publishedAtEtMeta has no time-of-day gate on the STAMP it parses, unlike its isInEditionWindow/inNighthawkEditionCatchupAlertWindow siblings in the same file which ARE confirmed latent), confirmed it's a real bug: a published_at genuinely stamped 00:00-00:59 ET on 'today' would compute minutes=1440-1499 instead of 0-59, making shouldRebuildStalePublishedEdition wrongly skip a rebuild it should trigger. Branched (fix/edition-stale-midnight-hour24), RED->GREEN (2 new tests, both failed pre-fix), applied the same %24 normalisation #4703 used, full Night Hawk suite 1358/1358 pass, tsc clean. PR #4715 opened (draft), subscribed. Per the now-rescinded CARVE-OUT, will merge directly once CI is green -- no Cursor sign-off wait.

AGGRESSIVE-HUNT investigation instead of a 4th redundant API poll (nothing had changed for ~15min and picks can't resolve until market opens ~7h out). Pulled the FULL raw play objects (not just the fields my own probe script had been cherry-picking) -- found rich server-computed data already present: factor_breakdown (12-dimension score components), tier.factors (human-readable tier reasoning), confirming_signals, target_atr_multiple, rr_ratio. Noticed SIG/ASO rr_ratio=0.35 labeled 'tight' and FICO rr_ratio=0.72 labeled 'acceptable' in the thesis text -- looked like a possible mislabeling (0.72 reward:risk is objectively a below-breakeven ratio). Traced to source (play-levels.ts computeRiskReward + deterministic-edition.ts's rrLabel bands) and found this is NOT a new bug: it's the deliberate, already-documented output of the 2026-08-06 win-rate presentation-only recalibration campaign (see FINDINGS.md same date) -- the function's own code comment explains the edge-basis R:R was intentionally made MORE honest (lower) than the old mid-basis number specifically because 20/48 plays in a July-Aug window had fill-edge R:R below 1.0 that the old display concealed. Confirmed system working as designed, not a defect. Useful cycle even though nothing shipped: ruled out a plausible-looking false lead before it became a wasted PR, and confirmed the live edition IS populating the richer scoring fields server-side (factor_breakdown/tier.factors/confirming_signals/target_atr_multiple) -- worth checking on a future cycle whether the member-facing UI actually renders all of these or whether some are computed-but-unsurfaced (did not check the UI render this cycle, API-only).
